title: Scraping (Knockdown)
short_answer: After hang, before tape: knock down high edges, proud screws, and loose paper so the first coat has a fair plane.
summary: The cheapest labor in the entire drywall sequence, and it directly replaces the most expensive. This is why it's a tracked stage of its own.
when_to_use: You can see proud joints, torn paper, or high fasteners
plain_words: Before the tapers come in, somebody walks every room with a knife and cleans it up — shave the bumps off the seams, set every proud screw, cut out the boxes that got missed, sweep out the scrap. Then between coats, you shave the ridges off while the mud is still soft. That's it. It's simple work and it saves more time than almost anything else we do.

steps.body: Run a knife over every seam and edge — knock off crumbs, dust ridges, and loose torn paper.
Check every screw. Proud ones get set. Broken-paper ones get a new screw beside them.
Find and cut the missed openings — boxes, sprinkler drops, access panels. Found here, not by an electrician with a hammer.
Knock down high spots at butt joints and anywhere board isn't sitting flat.
Pre-fill oversized gaps and voids with setting compound now, so the taper isn't building a bridge.
Clear scrap and debris out of the room and off the floor.
Walk it the way the taper will: if you'd have to stop and fix something, fix it now.
Every seam and edge clean of crumbs and loose paper.
Every screw set; broken ones addressed.
All openings cut, including the missed ones.
Floor clear of scrap and cured mud.
A taper could start without stopping. Scrapping Status updated.

warnings.title: Over-sanding into the core
warnings.body: Scraping is knockdown, not leveling the whole wall. Digging into gypsum weakens the face for tape.

warnings.title: Job Check label
warnings.body: Monday calls this Scrapping Status — same pass as scrape/knockdown in the Field Manual.

variations.title: Clean hang
variations.when: Board landed well and fasteners are consistent
changes: Short walk + vacuum may be enough
Still check butts and cutouts before tape

quality_checks.prompt: No proud or torn-paper screw heads left for tape
Plane free of crumbs and loose paper

common_mistakes.title: Skipping scrape on a rough hang
common_mistakes.wrong: Go straight to tape over proud edges
common_mistakes.why: First coat bridges highs and fails early

troubleshooting.symptom: Tape blisters at butts after first coat
troubleshooting.likely_cause: Debris or loose paper left on plane

provenance.note: Aligned with Job Check Scrapping Status. Spelling on Monday is Scrapping; field language is scrape/knockdown.
